summary: Depth-first rabbithole dossier for Multi-Document Transactions; source-anchored research pack.

facts.text: [high] Read operations inside a transaction are not guaranteed to see writes performed by other committed transactions or non-transactional writes, and may read now-deleted documents due to using a snapshot from before the write operation. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions-production-consideration.md, https://severalnines.com/blog/transaction-considerations-mongodb-production/

[low] Because transactions hold collection locks, DDL operations such as index builds can queue behind them, extending transaction duration and snapshot lifetime. Sources: https://www.netdata.cloud/guides/mongodb/mongodb-long-running-transactions/

[low] When connecting to MongoDB Server version 4.2 or earlier, write operations in a transaction can only be performed on collections that already exist, whereas in version 4.4 and later, the server automatically creates collections as necessary. (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/crud/transactions.md

[low] Transactions that exceed transactionLifetimeLimitSeconds are considered expired and are aborted by a periodic cleanup process, which runs every transactionLifetimeLimitSeconds/2 seconds or at least once every 60 seconds. The minimum value of transactionLifetimeLimitSeconds is 1 second. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md

[low] There are optimizations around when 2PC can be bypassed, such as for read-only transactions or for transactions that only write to a single shard. Sources: https://mongodb.com/company/blog/engineering/formal-methods-beyond-correctness-isolation-permissiveness-distributed-transactions

[low] The dirty cache is limited to 20% of the total cache size, and when transactionTooLargeForCacheThreshold is set to 0.75, the server only retries transactions that use less than 15% of the total storage engine cache. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md

[low] In a history containing roughly 100 transactions per second, 1461 out of 13914 total transactions were identified with cyclic dependencies, and roughly 10% of transactions exhibited anomalies during normal operation without faults. (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://jepsen.io/analyses/mongodb-4.2.6

[high] If a multi-document transaction is in progress, new DDL operations affecting the same database or collection wait behind the transaction, and non-transactional operations accessing the same resources block until they reach their maxTimeMS limit. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions-production-consideration.md, https://severalnines.com/blog/transaction-considerations-mongodb-production/

[medium] You cannot write to capped collections, read/write to collections in the config, admin, or local databases, or write to system.* collections within a transaction. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions-operations.md
[low] You cannot return the supported operation's query plan using explain or similar commands within a transaction. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md

[high] You cannot create new collections in cross-shard write transactions, and MongoDB does not support collection operations such as collection creation within a transaction unless specific conditions are met. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions-operations.md, https://docs.spring.io/spring-data/mongodb/reference/mongodb/client-session-transactions.html
[low] You cannot use the $graphLookup stage within a transaction while targeting a sharded collection. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md

[low] The server responds with error 50851 when issuing a count command inside a multi-document transaction, as MongoDB count operates on collection statistics which may not reflect the actual situation within a transaction. Sources: https://docs.spring.io/spring-data/mongodb/reference/mongodb/client-session-transactions.html

[low] The count of open transactions is server-wide, and process-internal transactions are exempt from rejection but still contribute to the total count when the server enforces the limit for external clients. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md
[low] Set the parameter to 0 to disable the limit on open transactions, as the minimum value is 0. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md

MongoDB documentation and tutorial blog posts show only write-only transactions using read concern local rather than snapshot, while Learn MongoDB The Hard Way uses read concern snapshot but write concern local despite performing writes. Sources: https://jepsen.io/analyses/mongodb-4.2.6

[medium] MongoDB supports ACID multi-document transactions on replica sets and sharded clusters, providing atomicity, consistency, isolation, and durability based on configured read and write concerns. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/best-practices.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/crud/transactions.md

[high] Multi-document transactions require MongoDB Server version 4.0 or later, with standalone replica set transactions introduced in 4.0 and cross-shard transactions extended in 2019. (verified as of 2026-10-14) Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/crud/transactions.md, https://jepsen.io/analyses/mongodb-4.2.6, https://help.aliyun.com/en/mongodb/use-cases/transactions-and-read-write-concern

[low] Multi-document transactions pin WiredTiger snapshots until commit or abort, preventing the storage engine from evicting old document versions visible to that snapshot. Sources: https://www.netdata.cloud/guides/mongodb/mongodb-long-running-transactions/
[low] Individual operations within multi-document transactions never return TemporarilyUnavailable errors. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md

[low] MongoDB implements a distributed, multi-document transaction protocol that provides snapshot isolation for transactions issued by clients using a general, interactive transactional interface. Sources: https://mongodb.com/company/blog/engineering/formal-methods-beyond-correctness-isolation-permissiveness-distributed-transactions

[low] Transactions are built on top of Sessions and require an active ClientSession, which enables the Causal Consistency model to guarantee operations respect causal relationships. Sources: https://docs.spring.io/spring-data/mongodb/reference/mongodb/client-session-transactions.html

[medium] A session is checked out from a session pool to run database operations, and a session can have at most one open transaction at a time. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/reference/parameters.md

[low] If a session ends with an open transaction, the transaction aborts, and all data changes made in the transaction are discarded without ever becoming visible. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md

[high] Until a transaction commits, data changes made within it are not visible outside the transaction, although the transaction can read its own uncommitted writes. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md, https://help.aliyun.com/en/mongodb/use-cases/transactions-and-read-write-concern

[high] Transactions lock documents they modify, blocking other operations until completion, and if a write outside the transaction modifies a document the transaction is modifying, the transaction aborts due to a write conflict. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions-production-consideration.md, https://help.aliyun.com/en/mongodb/use-cases/transactions-and-read-write-concern, https://severalnines.com/blog/transaction-considerations-mongodb-production/, https://www.mongodb.com/community/forums/t/issues-mongodb-transactions-pessimistic-locking/118377

[low] If two concurrent transactions try to update the same key at the same shard, one of them will be forced to abort due to standard write-conflict checking behavior of snapshot isolation. Sources: https://mongodb.com/company/blog/engineering/formal-methods-beyond-correctness-isolation-permissiveness-distributed-transactions

[low] Operations in a transaction use the transaction-level read concern, ignoring any read concern set at the collection or database level, and transactions without an explicit read concern downgrade requested levels to local. Sources: https://jepsen.io/analyses/mongodb-4.2.6

[low] To obtain snapshot isolation, users must set the read concern to snapshot and the write concern to majority for each transaction, even for read-only transactions. Sources: https://jepsen.io/analyses/mongodb-4.2.6

[low] The 'snapshot' read concern provides standard snapshot isolation for transactions, while the 'local' read concern provides a weaker isolation level similar to read-committed. Sources: https://mongodb.com/company/blog/engineering/formal-methods-beyond-correctness-isolation-permissiveness-distributed-transactions

[medium] Write operations inside transactions must be run without an explicit write concern specification and use the default write concern; the transaction-level write concern is applied at commit. If it is unset at transaction and session level, it defaults to the client-level write concern, which is w: "majority" in MongoDB 5.0 and later (with differences for deployments with arbiters) and w: 1 otherwise. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/drivers/node/current/crud/transactions.md

[low] Transactions containing read operations must use read preference 'primary', and all operations in a given transaction must route to the same member. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md

[medium] For explicit creation of a collection or index inside a transaction, the transaction read concern level must be 'local', and the index must be on a non-existing collection or a new empty collection created earlier in the same transaction. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions-operations.md

[low] The distributed transactions protocol in MongoDB uses causally consistent timestamps across a sharded cluster for managing ordering and visibility between transactions. Sources: https://mongodb.com/company/blog/engineering/formal-methods-beyond-correctness-isolation-permissiveness-distributed-transactions

[low] Through snapshot isolation, transactions provide a consistent view of data, enforce all-or-nothing execution, and do not impact performance for workloads that do not require them. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/blog/post/performance-best-practices-transactions-and-read--write-concerns

[high] In MongoDB, a write operation is atomic on the level of a single document, and one or more fields may be written in a single operation, including updates to multiple subdocuments and elements of an array. Sources: https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/core/transactions.md, https://www.mongodb.com/docs/manual/data-modeling/best-practices.md, https://www.mongodb.com/blog/post/performance-best-practices-transactions-and-read--write-concerns

Tutorials from DZone, Several Nines, Percona, The Code Barbarian, and Spring.io claim transactions are ACID or offer snapshot isolation, but none set either read or write concern, conflicting with the requirement to set both for snapshot isolation. Sources: https://jepsen.io/analyses/mongodb-4.2.6
